A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite changed titles and terminology. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original architecture-benchmark measurements, proxy correlations, NAS comparisons, ablations, and image-benchmark transfer experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original NAS experiments and adds predictive-performance, runtime, and broader-search-space evaluations.

M1.justification: The filter-and-refine framework persists after ATLAS/ExpressFlow become pTNAS/pTProxy. However, v3 replaces trajectory-length normalization with finite-difference layer sensitivity and adds residual and heterogeneous block architectures with corresponding insertion, deletion, and attribute mutations (Sections 3.2–3.3; Appendix D.4). These changes materially broaden the search procedure.

E1.justification: Frappe, Diabetes, and Criteo remain. V3 adds eight main relational classification/regression tasks from Event, Beer, Trial, Avito, and H&M, plus Avito ad-ctr and H&M user-churn in Appendix D.4. The four image-NAS benchmark evaluations in v2 Table 15 are removed.

E2.justification: V3 Tables 2 and 16 newly evaluate LR, RF, CatBoost, LightGBM, TabPFN, TabICL, DNN, DeepFM, FTTrans, ARM-Net, TP-BERTa, Nomic, and BGE against pTNAS. The earlier NAS and proxy comparisons are largely retained, with RE-NAS renamed EA-NAS.

E3.justification: New comparisons introduce temporal evaluation, 10-second NAS budgets, AUC/MAE metrics, capped training, and early stopping. For the retained benchmark, v3 Appendix D.1 reports size-bucket-specific training configurations, whereas v2 Appendix C.2 specifies one configuration per dataset. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of proxy ranking and search generalization to ResDNN and BlockMixed, including selected-architecture examples (Appendix D.4). V2's image-transfer and all-ones-input analyses disappear. Most initialization, batch-size, recalibration, noise, and coordinator ablations remain under new appendix numbering.

E5.justification: V3 Figure 10 newly reports mean search performance over five random seeds for the additional search spaces. Table 1 adds SRCC standard deviations across datasets, not across runs. The earlier 100-run strategy comparisons and five-repeat batch-size experiments retain their reported run counts.

E6.justification: New Tables 16–17 report predictive and runtime results, including pTNAS's overall average rank of 1.38 and regression total time of 33.53 seconds versus TabPFN's 160.24 seconds. The original 82.75× NAS speedup remains. Some SRCC entries and ranks change, including SynFlow's average rank from 2.6 to 2.3; image-transfer and all-ones results are removed.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix E corrects the earlier saliency derivation by counting the bias once and preserving neuron-wise absolute values and layer weights in the final aggregation. It also defines finite-difference sensitivity and replaces the exact floor-log refinement-cost expression with an approximate ceiling-log expression. The underlying saliency argument remains.

C1.justification: V2's central empirical claims concern anytime NAS and search acceleration. V3 retains these ideas but additionally claims the best average predictive rank and end-to-end efficiency advantages over TabPFN, positioning dataset-specific DNNs as competitive alternatives to tabular foundation models (Abstract, Introduction, and Conclusion).

C2.justification: V3 adds substantial interpretations of accuracy and latency differences among model families, explains task restrictions such as TabICL's classification-only applicability, and acknowledges that pTNAS is not always fastest on classification. Its conclusion adds memory footprint as an unaddressed deployment constraint. Earlier data-agnostic and image-transfer interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: V3 adds split counts, historical relational-feature construction, training caps, early-stopping settings, and broader search-space options (Appendices C–D). The stated reproduction repository changes from Trails to pTNAS. Conversely, v2's explicit all-ones proxy-loss recipe and worker-queue pseudocode are no longer provided.

R1.justification: V3 substantially repositions the work around foundation-model accuracy/latency trade-offs, adding TabPFN, TabICL, recent NAS literature, an explicit comparison with PNAS, and connections to NeurDB. V2 primarily positions the contribution around anytime NAS and replacing manual tabular architecture design.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten alongside the method renaming. Benchmark characterization moves from the main experiments to Appendix D, notation moves from Appendix H to A, and the appendices are reorganized around setup, theory, analyses, and complete results.

P2.justification: V3 adopts two-column main text, replaces the generic NAS overview with dedicated search-space and workflow diagrams, and adds predictive-performance, runtime, and mixed-architecture displays. Retained benchmark figures move to appendices, ten proxy-correlation figures become five paired figures, and the SRCC table is restructured into summaries.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses v2's limited practical validation through direct predictive/runtime comparisons with tabular model families and tests beyond fixed-depth MLPs. Expanded setup information and corrected saliency derivations further improve assessability. These gains outweigh removal of the image-transfer and data-agnostic analyses. Important documentation weaknesses remain: Table 6 does not supply the claimed size-specific configurations, and matching a 10-second NAS budget does not match total fitting time.
